{{machine learning bar}}
In [[computer science]], a '''logistic model tree''' ('''LMT''') is a [[statistical classification|classification]] model with an associated [[supervised learning|supervised training]] [[algorithm]] that combines [[logistic regression]] (LR) and [[decision tree learning]].<ref name="ecml03">{{cite conference |author1=Niels Landwehr |author2=Mark Hall |author3=Eibe Frank |url=http://www.cs.waikato.ac.nz/~ml/publications/2003/landwehr-etal.pdf |title=Logistic model trees |year=2003 |conference=[[ECML PKDD]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Landwehr | first1 = N.| last2 = Hall | first2 = M.| last3 = Frank | first3 = E.| title = Logistic Model Trees | doi = 10.1007/s10994-005-0466-3 | journal = Machine Learning | volume = 59 | pages = 161–205 | year = 2005 | issue = 1–2| url = http://www.cs.waikato.ac.nz/~eibe/pubs/LMT.pdf| doi-access = free }}</ref>

Logistic model trees are based on the earlier idea of a model tree: a decision tree that has [[linear regression]] models at its leaves to provide a [[Piecewise linear function|piecewise linear]] regression model (where ordinary decision trees with constants at their leaves would produce a piecewise constant model).<ref name="ecml03"/> In the logistic variant, the [[LogitBoost]] algorithm is used to produce an LR model at every node in the tree; the node is then split using the [[C4.5 algorithm|C4.5]] criterion. Each LogitBoost invocation is warm-started{{vague|date=October 2016}} from its results in the parent node. Finally, the tree is pruned.<ref name="pkdd05">{{cite conference |author1=Sumner, Marc |author2=Eibe Frank |author3=Mark Hall |title=Speeding up logistic model tree induction |conference=PKDD |publisher=Springer |year=2005 |pages=675–683 |url=http://www.cs.waikato.ac.nz/~ml/publications/2005/SumnerFrankHallCameraReady.pdf}}</ref>

The basic LMT induction algorithm uses [[cross-validation (statistics)|cross-validation]] to find a number of LogitBoost iterations that does not [[overfitting|overfit]] the training data. A faster version has been proposed that uses the [[Akaike information criterion]] to control LogitBoost stopping.<ref name="pkdd05"/>
